details:
Summary

My avatar uses Native Face Tracking with Eye Gaze Mode set to "Bone Rotation." With Selfie Expression (webcam), the eyes move through the full configured range. With tracking through VRCFT, the eye movement range becomes extremely narrow.

Environment

・VRChat build: 1953

・VRCFT version: 6.0.0

・Modules / devices: iPhone, Quest Pro, Bigscreen Beyond, Virtual Desktop

・Platform: PC (Windows)

Avatar setup

・Eye Gaze Mode: Bone Rotation

 > Horizontal (left/right): 6°

 > Vertical (up/down): 4°

・Face Tracking: "Use All Tracking Keys" enabled

・Native parameters connected to the Animator Controller parameters via Parameter Behaviors

・The face tracking itself is driven by the Animator Controller

Steps to reproduce

1. Use an avatar with the setup above (avtr_66029737-50fe-4e4c-b330-d456bbc57b90)

2. Start VRCFT with eye tracking enabled

3. Look far left/right and up/down

Expected behavior

The eyes rotate through the configured range (6° horizontal, 4° vertical), the same as with Selfie Expression.

Actual behavior

The eye rotation range is far smaller than configured (see attached video).

Isolation results

・Selfie Expression (webcam) + Native Face Tracking (Bone Rotation): works correctly

・Older OSC-based face tracking (before native support) + VRCFT: works correctly

・A different avatar without Native Face Tracking (avtr_2988d5c9-f42a-4cf9-bf13-4175589d52d5) + VRCFT: works correctly

・Native Face Tracking (Bone Rotation) + VRCFT: range is reduced

As far as I can tell, the issue only happens with this combination of Native Face Tracking (Bone Rotation) and VRCFT.

Test avatars

・Native Face Tracking avatar: avtr_66029737-50fe-4e4c-b330-d456bbc57b90

・VRCFT (OSC) face tracking avatar, for comparison: avtr_2988d5c9-f42a-4cf9-bf13-4175589d52d5
title: Eye gaze range is severely reduced when using Native Face Tracking (Eye Gaze Mode: Bone Rotation) via VRCFT
